VLA Beginner Docs — a reading list

August 17, 2026 robotics,, VLA,, LeRobot,, beginner,, docs

Start with LeRobot docs and Colabs, not the 7B papers. ACT first (imitation learning), then SmolVLA (your first real VLA). The VLA basics note is the concept map; this page is the official docs in a sensible order.

Read in this order

1. Concepts (no GPU, no robot)

Doc Why
🤗 Robotics Course — welcome Beginner syllabus. Python is enough. Units 5–7 (RL / IL / foundation models) are still rolling out.
Unit 1 — robot learning Why we train from data instead of writing a planner.
Unit 1 — what LeRobot is The library you will actually run.
Robot Learning Tutorial Longer companion (classical robotics → RL → imitation → foundation models). Skim until you need depth.

2. Install and the CLI map

Doc Why
LeRobot docs home The four-step loop: teleoperate → record → train → deploy. Pick “I have a robot” or “no hardware yet.”
Installation Python ≥ 3.12. Use extras: core_scripts to record, training to train, feetech for SO-100/SO-101.
Cheat sheet Copy-paste lerobot-record, lerobot-train, lerobot-rollout. Keep this tab open.

3. First policy: ACT (do this before any VLA)

ACT is the recommended first policy: small, fast to train, same data format as SmolVLA.

Doc Why
ACT policy What action chunking is, plus the lerobot-train --policy.type=act command.
Imitation learning on real robots End-to-end on hardware: teleop, record, train ACT, evaluate.
Train ACT Colab No local GPU. ~1.5 h / 100k steps on an A100; a T4 works, slower.

4. First VLA: SmolVLA

Only after ACT clones a tiny skill (pick-and-place one object).

Doc Why
SmolVLA docs 450M VLA. Fine-tune lerobot/smolvla_base on ~50 of your episodes.
SmolVLA blog Architecture in plain language (VLM + flow-matching action expert).
Train SmolVLA Colab Same Hub dataset workflow as the ACT notebook. ~5 h / 20k steps on an A100.
Notebooks index Official Colab list.

5. If you have (or will buy) an arm

Doc Why
SO-101 assembly Flagship cheap arm: motors, calibrate, then jump to the IL tutorial.
LeLab GUI Browser app for SO-101: calibrate, record, train, deploy without memorizing CLI.
Cameras Find OpenCV / RealSense devices. Wrist + scene beats one laptop webcam.
What makes a good dataset Two steady views, ~30 FPS, leader arm out of frame, ~50 episodes, a real task sentence not task1.

Target: grasp an object in a few locations and drop it in a bin. Hugging Face suggests ≥ 50 episodes, ~10 per location. You should be able to do the task yourself using only the camera feeds.

Weekend path (no robot)

  1. Robotics Course unit 0 + unit 1.
  2. Install: pip install 'lerobot[training]' (or just open Colab).
  3. Train ACT on a Hub dataset, e.g. something under lerobot on the Hub.
  4. Read the SmolVLA page and run the SmolVLA Colab on the same kind of dataset.

Weekend path (SO-101 on the desk)

  1. SO-101 or LeLab.
  2. Teleop until the motion is boringly consistent.
  3. Record ~50 pick-and-place episodes (IL tutorial + dataset checklist).
  4. Train ACT. If success is near zero, fix data/cameras — do not jump to a VLA.
  5. Fine-tune SmolVLA on the same dataset.

Save for later (not beginner)

These are real, but they assume you already have a working imitation loop.

  • π0 in LeRobot — flow-matching VLA, heavier than SmolVLA.
  • OpenVLA 7B model card — load + predict_action. Needs a serious GPU; LoRA fine-tune is a separate repo.
  • OpenVLA GitHub — research training, not the first clone-and-train.
  • Open X-Embodiment — the big multi-robot pretraining corpus.

Community

  • LeRobot Discord — install, cameras, and “why is success 0%” questions.
  • Hub search: datasets tagged LeRobot.
